THE BUG -- THE BLIND-BOT DETECTOR CRIED WOLF EVERY NIGHT. The _check_scan_stale() detector added 2026-08-27 measures WALL-CLOCK time since the last completed scan against SCAN_STALE_ALERT_SEC=8100 (2h15m). But the main loop has two SCHEDULED scan-free windows, and the detector counted both as outage:
  (a) OFF-SESSION. `if not in_session(h): continue` (S1 inheritance, session 11:00-24:00) returns to the top of the loop before _mark_scan_ok() was ever reached, so the clock starved for 11h every night. Evidence in bot.log: alert 08-28 01:17, recovery 11:01; alert 08-29 01:17, recovery 11:01 -- recovery lands exactly at the session boundary. The same defect delayed the REAL 08-27 outage's recovery notice by ~9h (alert 04:25, bot actually healthy ~05:00, 'recovered' DM not sent until 11:01).
  (b) QUIET HOURS. 02:00-04:00 is a deliberate 2h scanning pause. The check skips WHILE quiet, then wakes at 04:00 having accrued 3.0h of 'staleness'. Evidence: 08-30 04:00:46 'Bot blind: no scan completed in 3.0h' followed by 'Scanning recovered' at 04:01:42 -- 56 seconds later.

Net effect: 3 of the 4 blind alerts ever sent were false, and the pattern was a nightly alarm-then-all-clear pair. That is precisely the alarm fatigue that let the real 08-27 outage read as noise. A liveness threshold must be measured against the schedule the system actually promises, not against the wall clock.

FIXED in live.py, three parts: (1) _mark_scan_ok() moved to immediately after the watchlist scan loop and gated on `states` being non-empty -- it now means 'prices were actually returned this candle', which is strictly stronger than the old placement and is above both gates; (2) new _unscheduled_stale_seconds() discounts quiet-hours seconds from the staleness clock, deriving the window from should_quiet() rather than re-hardcoding 2-4 (this repo has had three stale-instrument bugs in a fortnight); (3) _check_scan_stale() now takes ONE clock reading for both the hour gate and the arithmetic -- it was reading datetime.now() and time.time() separately, which is both a boundary race and why the function was untestable.

Verified: a real outage spanning quiet hours (08-27 geometry: last scan 00:01, check 04:30) STILL alerts -- adjusted staleness 2.48h > 2.25h limit. test_scan_stale.py extended 15 -> 27 assertions, all pass, including a source-order assertion that the marker precedes the off-session continue (no amount of stubbing catches an ordering bug).
